title: Toolbar select overflow: global `select{width:100%}` wins over flex:0 0 auto unless width is reset
trigger: A `.toolbar` (or any flex-row) child element uses `flex: 0 0 auto` but visually still stretches to fill/overflow its flex container in src/ui/public/index.html.
behavior_delta: In src/ui/public/index.html, a generic rule (`input, textarea, select { width: 100%; ... }`) applied to every select on the page, including the compact toolbar filters. `.toolbar select { ...; flex: 0 0 auto; }` set a flex-basis of auto but never set `width`, and flex-basis:auto defers to the element's own `width` property -- so `width: 100%` from the generic rule still won, and each toolbar select tried to claim the full toolbar width (observed: toolbar rendered ~300vw wide with 3 such selects). Fix was a one-line addition of `width: auto;` to `.toolbar select`. General lesson: when giving a flex item `flex: 0 0 auto` (or any basis of `auto`) to make it size to content, always check for a competing `width` rule elsewhere in the cascade -- flex-basis:auto silently falls back to it, and the flex shorthand alone does not shrink an explicitly-widened element.

General lesson: when giving a flex item `flex: 0 0 auto` (or any basis of `auto`) to make it size to content, always check for a competing `width` rule elsewhere in the cascade -- flex-basis:auto silently falls back to it, and the flex shorthand alone does not shrink an explicitly-widened element.
why: User reported the toolbar select filters were huge / the toolbar was using ~300vw. Traced to the CSS cascade interaction described above and fixed directly in src/ui/public/index.html.
